title: Crestline Business Points Earning Chart
content:
Crestline Business points are the company points of Crestline Corporate Travel Agreements. The earning chart below gives, for every tier, the earning rate, the treatment of the traveler's own Summit miles and of partner-operated flights, the window for retroactive claims and the validity of earned points.

| Tier | Business points per US dollar of eligible flown spend | Traveler also earns personal Summit miles on the same flight | Partner-operated flights earn business points | Retroactive claim window (calendar days after the flight) | Points expire after (calendar months after the month of earning) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Crestline Business Connect | 1 | yes | no | 30 | 24 |
| Crestline Business Connect Plus | 1 | yes | no | 30 | 24 |
| Crestline Corporate Select | 1.5 | yes | no | 60 | 24 |
| Crestline Corporate Preferred | 2 | yes | no | 60 | 36 |
| Crestline Corporate Premier | 2 | yes | no | 90 | 36 |
| Crestline Corporate Strategic | 3 | yes | no | 90 | 36 |

### Footnotes to the chart

1. The earning rate is stated in business points per US dollar of eligible flown spend; Crestline Corporate Select earns one and a half points per dollar.
2. On every tier the traveler also earns personal Summit miles in the Crestline Summit Loyalty Program on the same flight; business points and Summit miles are separate balances.
3. On no tier do partner-operated flights earn business points.
4. The retroactive claim window is the number of calendar days after the flight within which points may be claimed for an eligible ticket that was booked without the agreement.
5. The expiry figure is the number of calendar months after the month in which points were earned; unredeemed points expire at the end of that later month.
